title: West Yorkshire Police's first live facial recognition deployment in Huddersfield: three arrests, including a domestic stalking suspect, and six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks over three days
summary: Examiner and BBC (17 Aug 2026): two LFR vans in Huddersfield town center over three days led to three arrests and six Sexual Harm Prevention Order stops; the stalking suspect was among those arrested.
account: West Yorkshire Police used two live facial recognition (LFR) vans in Huddersfield town center for the first time. The three-day operation ran the week before 17 August 2026, with two vans on the Wednesday and one on the Thursday and Friday. The Huddersfield Examiner reported it on 17 August. The cameras compare live images with a watchlist and generate alerts that officers review before acting. Non-matching faces are deleted in seconds. The deployment led to three arrests. They were a man wanted on suspicion of domestic stalking, a person wanted on warrant and a person wanted for shoplifting offenses. Six people subject to Sexual Harm Prevention Orders were stopped and spoken with (Examiner, BBC). Inspector Mark Pattinson of Kirklees Police said its first use in Kirklees “has delivered real results”. Chief Inspector Dan Tillett, the force's LFR lead, said the force is “not using it for mass surveillance or indiscriminate monitoring”. The BBC notes criticism from civil liberty groups.
purpose: LFR vans are deployed to match passers-by against a watchlist of wanted people and suspects so that officers can arrest or check them. The arrests and order checks are that purpose. The Examiner adds that the cameras also serve to find missing people, witnesses and victims.
system: West Yorkshire Police live facial recognition (LFR) cameras mounted on vans
segment: Live facial recognition in a town center

ratings.reason: Kirklees Police arrested three wanted people, including a domestic stalking suspect, and checked six people under Sexual Harm Prevention Orders in three days. The figures are the force's statements in the Examiner and BBC. It is a measurable result for the district.

Residents: a stalking suspect, a person on warrant and a shoplifting suspect were detained, and six order subjects were checked. No report shows a specific harm prevented, so the public benefit is the enforcement itself.

ai_role.statement: The LFR system generated the alerts. The Examiner and BBC say live images were compared against a watchlist and matches were reviewed by trained officers before any action. The identification is the system's, and the arrests are officers' work. No vendor, false-alert count or number of faces scanned is given, and all outcome figures come from West Yorkshire Police.
